I located the fault, but did not implement the fix: this run was restricted to diagnosis and prohibited edits to project source or tests.

The main change belongs in [lib/utils/parse/parse.go](/app/lib/utils/parse/parse.go:38). `Expression` holds only one variable and one transform; `walk` drops an inner transform when parsing a nested call, so nested `email.local` and `regexp.replace` cannot compose. The same walk flattens selectors and indices without checking their shape or namespace, accepts literals as variable parts, and returns inconsistent errors for malformed expressions. Its depth check runs after Go has already parsed the input.

[ApplyValueTraits](/app/lib/services/role.go:491) and [PAM interpolation](/app/lib/srv/ctx.go:973) validate only the single variable exposed by that structure. They need validation for every variable in the proposed AST. PAM’s missing trait warning also includes the claim name.

The fix should replace the parser result with typed string and boolean AST nodes, validate variable shape and function arguments during parsing, evaluate nested string expressions, and use the same compiled regex path for matching and replacement. Existing [parser tests](/app/lib/utils/parse/parse_test.go:28) pass (`go test ./lib/utils/parse`), but assert the legacy concrete structs and do not establish the requested nested behavior. I recorded the findings in `.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md`; project source and tests are untouched.

Implemented a typed expression AST in [lib/utils/parse](/app/lib/utils/parse/ast.go). Parsing now supports nested string functions, constant inputs, strict variable shapes and namespaces, typed matcher predicates, and bounded template parsing. Trait and PAM interpolation validate each variable through a callback.

`go test ./lib/utils/parse` passes, and `git diff --check` is clean. I could not complete the broader `lib/services` and `lib/srv` tests: the local build lacks `linux/hidraw.h`, and disabling CGO causes HID, PKCS#11, and BPF compile errors.

VERDICT: FIX

**Code defect:** [splitTemplate](/app/lib/utils/parse/parse.go:75) rejects ordinary single braces in plain literals and static template text. For example, `NewExpression("a{b}")` and `NewMatcher("a{b}")` now return malformed-template errors, although neither contains a `{{` or `}}` delimiter. Allow single braces and reject malformed double delimiters.

**Tests run:** `GOPROXY=off go test ./lib/utils/parse` and `GOPROXY=off go test ./lib/services` passed.

**TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM:** `go test ./lib/utils/parse ./lib/services ./lib/srv` exited 1: `lib/srv` could not build because `linux/hidraw.h` is missing and sqlite3 lacks `pread64`/`off64_t`. `GOPROXY=off CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./lib/srv` also exited 1 on missing platform symbols. The `lib/srv` tests therefore did not execute; its native build dependencies need to be available before that package can be verified.

Fixed the brace parsing defect in [parse.go](/app/lib/utils/parse/parse.go): ordinary single braces now work in literals and static text around templates, while malformed `{{` and `}}` delimiters still produce errors. Added regression cases in [parse_test.go](/app/lib/utils/parse/parse_test.go).

The reviewer’s exact `GOPROXY=off go test` commands for `./lib/utils/parse` and `./lib/services` pass. `git diff --check` passes.

**TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM:** `./lib/srv` could not build because `linux/hidraw.h` and required sqlite3 symbols are unavailable. The CGO disabled retry also failed on missing platform symbols, so its tests did not run.
